explanation: Newton’s Second Law states that the force acting on an object is equal to its mass multiplied by its acceleration.
Linear search checks each element in a list one by one until the desired value is found or the list ends.
Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in the data.
A queue follows the First In First Out principle, similar to people waiting in a line.
Kirchhoff’s laws describe how current and voltage behave in electrical circuits based on conservation principles.
Iteration is the process of repeating a set of instructions until a condition is met.
A computer network connects multiple devices so they can share data and resources.
Big-O notation describes the upper bound of an algorithm’s time or space requirements as input size grows.
The mean is the average of values, while the median is the middle value when data is ordered.
Normalization organizes database tables to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.
The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed.
Selection sort repeatedly selects the smallest element from the unsorted part and moves it to the sorted part.
Regularization reduces overfitting by adding a penalty for large model parameters.
A tree is a hierarchical data structure with a root node and child nodes forming parent-child relationships.
Faraday’s Law states that a changing magnetic field induces an electromotive force in a conductor.
Loops allow a block of code to run repeatedly until a condition is satisfied.
The Internet Protocol is responsible for addressing and routing data packets across networks.
Expected value represents the average outcome of a random process over many trials.
A functional dependency describes the relationship where one set of attributes determines another in a database.
Deadlock occurs when processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.
Impulse is the product of force and the time over which it acts, causing a change in momentum.
Insertion sort builds the sorted list one element at a time by inserting elements into their correct position.
The learning rate controls how much model parameters are adjusted during training.
A graph consists of vertices and edges used to represent relationships between entities.
Pascal’s Law states that pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.
Multithreading allows a program to execute multiple threads concurrently for better performance.
The Domain Name System translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
Standard deviation measures how spread out values are from the mean.
BCNF is a database normalization form that reduces redundancy by enforcing stricter functional dependencies.
Livelock occurs when processes continuously change state in response to each other without making progress.
In an elastic collision, both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
Bucket sort distributes elements into buckets, sorts each bucket, and then combines them.
A loss function measures how far a model’s predictions are from the actual values.
A binary tree is a tree data structure where each node has at most two children.
Archimedes’ principle states that an object immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of displaced fluid.
Context switching is the process of storing and restoring the state of a CPU so multiple processes can share it.
HTTP is a protocol used for transferring data over the web between clients and servers.
Variance measures how far values in a dataset are spread out from the mean.
Third Normal Form removes transitive dependencies to further reduce redundancy in database tables.
Starvation occurs when a process never gets required resources because others keep taking them.
Torque measures the tendency of a force to rotate an object around an axis.
Radix sort processes numbers digit by digit, grouping them based on place value.
PCA reduces dimensionality by transforming data into uncorrelated components that capture most variance.
A priority queue removes elements based on priority rather than insertion order.
The Poisson distribution models the number of events occurring in a fixed interval of time or space.
Process states describe the different stages a process goes through during execution in an operating system.
The determinant is a scalar value that provides information about a matrix, such as invertibility.
Network topologies describe the physical or logical arrangement of devices in a network.
Fourth Normal Form removes multivalued dependencies to further reduce redundancy.
Priority scheduling allocates CPU time to processes based on their priority levels.
Centripetal force keeps an object moving in a circular path by constantly pulling it toward the center.
Interpolation search estimates the position of a target value based on its value relative to the range.
Ensemble learning combines multiple models to improve prediction accuracy and robustness.
An adjacency matrix represents a graph using a matrix where entries indicate connections between vertices.
The harmonic mean is useful for averaging rates and is calculated as the reciprocal of the average of reciprocals.
Banker’s algorithm avoids deadlock by allocating resources only if the system remains in a safe state.
A critical section is a part of code that must not be executed by more than one thread at a time.
Matrix transpose is obtained by converting rows into columns and columns into rows.
Peer-to-peer networks allow devices to share resources directly without a central server.
Indexing improves database performance by enabling faster access to records using indexed attributes.
Coriolis force is an apparent force caused by the rotation of a reference frame, affecting moving objects.
Jump search moves ahead by fixed steps in a sorted array to locate a target efficiently.
The ROC curve shows the tradeoff between true positive rate and false positive rate across thresholds.
An incidence matrix represents relationships between vertices and edges in a graph.
The geometric mean is useful for averaging ratios and growth rates.
The readers-writers problem addresses synchronization when multiple readers and writers access shared data.
A semaphore is a synchronization tool that controls access to shared resources using counters.
LU decomposition factors a matrix into lower and upper triangular matrices for efficient solving.
Load balancing distributes workload across servers to improve performance and reliability.
MVCC allows concurrent database transactions by maintaining multiple versions of data items.
Precession is the gradual change in the orientation of a rotating object's axis.
Exponential search finds a range where the target lies and then applies binary search within it.
Precision measures correctness of positive predictions, while recall measures coverage of actual positives.
An adjacency list represents a graph by storing lists of neighbors for each vertex.
Root mean square provides an effective value for varying quantities, especially in signals.
The dining philosophers problem illustrates synchronization challenges when sharing limited resources.
A monitor is a synchronization construct that controls access to shared resources.
QR decomposition factors a matrix into an orthogonal matrix and an upper triangular matrix.
Circuit switching establishes a dedicated communication path before data transmission.
Snapshot isolation allows transactions to work on a consistent snapshot of the database.
Rolling motion combines both translational and rotational motion without slipping.
Fibonacci search uses Fibonacci numbers to divide the search space in a sorted array.
A confusion matrix summarizes prediction results by comparing actual and predicted classes.
A Cartesian tree combines heap and binary search tree properties based on array values.
A probability density function describes the likelihood of a continuous random variable taking a specific value.
Barrier synchronization forces threads to wait until all have reached a certain execution point.
CPM is a project management technique used to identify the longest sequence of dependent tasks.
Cholesky decomposition factors a matrix into a lower triangular matrix and its transpose.
Packet switching breaks data into packets that are routed independently across a network.
Serializable schedules ensure that concurrent transaction execution produces results equivalent to serial execution.
Relative velocity describes the velocity of one object as observed from the frame of reference of another object.
Ternary search divides a sorted array into three parts to locate a target value efficiently.
The F1 score balances precision and recall into a single performance measure.
A treap is a randomized data structure combining binary search tree and heap properties.
A cumulative distribution function gives the probability that a random variable is less than or equal to a value.
Lock-based concurrency controls access to shared resources using mutual exclusion locks.
Network latency is the time taken for data to travel from source to destination.
Eigen decomposition represents a matrix in terms of its eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
Message-oriented middleware enables asynchronous communication between distributed systems.
Recoverable schedules ensure that committed transactions depend only on other committed transactions.
